title: Does telling a learned view-synthesis blend which source is wrong help, or does it need to choose between the sources?
summary: Follow-up to capture-learngate. Two ways to close the gap to the best per-pixel blend were tried on the same toy scenes: four new features meant to say which warped source is wrong (signed depth order, and a cross-check that warps each source into the other's camera), and a second network that predicts a per-pixel mix of the two sources before the raw-camera blend. On 40 held-out scenes (new ground textures) the new features move the learned blend from 26.78 to 26.81 dB (+0.03, ahead in 35 of 40); the source weight moves it to 27.28 dB (+0.50 over learngate, ahead in 40 of 40), recovering 0.54 of the 2.71 dB hard-gate-to-best-blend headroom against 0.36 before. The gain comes from the second output, not the new features: with the old 12 features the source weight gets 27.24 dB. Outside the training ranges the gain shrinks to +0.04 dB over learngate. Toy analytic scene, block matcher, PSNR only; every scene parameter is drawn from stated ranges that are assumed, not sourced.
lede: does telling the blend model which of two sources is wrong help, or does it need to choose between them? New occlusion and cross-check features add 0.03 dB; a per-pixel source weight adds 0.47 dB (40 of 40 test configs), recovering 0.54 of the headroom to the best blend.
